question: Before opening a PR here, which of these tell you what it has to satisfy to be merged? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: A license sets what others may do with the code, not what a PR must contain.
CONTRIBUTING.md lists the written rules: tests required, black formatting, one issue per PR, and the branch naming pattern.
The PR template is the checklist you fill in when you open a PR. It makes the rules concrete at submission time.
ci.yml shows exactly which automated checks run on every PR — pytest and a black formatting check. A PR with either failing will not be merged.
Stars show popularity, not what a PR must contain.

question: You run #3's reproduction steps on the current code and nothing goes wrong, yet the issue is still open. Which explanation fits the repo's history?

options.text: The reporter was mistaken and it was never a bug.

options.text: A merged PR fixed it and the issue was never closed.

question: #8 is a one-line README typo — it looks perfect for a beginner. What should you check before taking it?

options.text: Whether it's already claimed or has an open PR.
options.explanation: Small issues get claimed quickly. A contributor commented on 2026-09-11 and opened draft PR #9 on 2026-09-12. Starting now would duplicate their work.

options.text: Whether docs fixes are accepted here.
options.explanation: The maintainer replied on 2026-09-06 saying typo fixes are welcome and even specified the branch naming. Docs contributions are clearly accepted.

options.text: Whether the same typo appears in other files too.
options.explanation: Checking for duplicate typos is reasonable after you confirm the issue is unclaimed. It's not what should come first.

options.text: Whether CI is green on the main branch.
options.explanation: CI status on main tells you about the repo's health, not whether someone already has this issue covered.

question: #6 says links break sometimes. The reporter says their markdown is in a large file and they can't paste it all. What's the most useful next step?
data_deps: issue {vagueIssueId} reporter reply says they can't paste the file

options.text: Rewrite the link handling and hope it covers the problem.
options.explanation: A fix without a reproduction case can't be checked. You might change behavior that was already correct.

options.text: Mark it "Reproduced" — the reporter has a file that breaks.
options.explanation: You have nothing you can run yourself. A file you can't see isn't a reproduction.

options.text: Close it, since the reporter has gone quiet.
options.explanation: Closing isn't your call, and the reporter may just need guidance on how to shrink the example.

options.text: Ask for the shortest input that still fails.
options.explanation: A whole file isn't a reproduction. Shrinking it to the smallest failing input is the standard move — and it's also how you isolate what's actually broken.

question: You're fixing #5. Which branch name follows this repo's rules?

options.explanation: No type prefix, and the description says nothing about what was changed.
Type prefix fix/, followed by a short description with hyphens. Matches the pattern shown in CONTRIBUTING.md exactly.

question: Your PR's CI run fails, and only on the black --check step. What do you do?
data_deps: ci.yml has a separate black --check step

options.text: Remove the black step from the CI workflow so it passes.
options.explanation: Changing the rules to make the check pass is not the same as following them. A reviewer would notice immediately.

options.text: Open a new PR with the formatting fixed.
options.explanation: That abandons the existing PR and its review thread. Fix and push to the same branch instead.

options.text: Run black, commit, push to the same branch.
options.explanation: Running black src/ tests/ locally, committing the formatted result, and pushing re-runs CI on the same PR. PR #7 shows exactly this: CI flagged formatting, the contributor fixed it and pushed, CI went green.

options.text: Ask a maintainer to merge it anyway.
options.explanation: That asks them to overlook a rule they set and enforced in CI. The fix takes one command.
